questions.q: A notebook costs ₹n. A pen costs ₹6 less than the notebook, and a geometry box costs twice as much as the notebook. Meera buys 3 notebooks, 2 pens and 1 geometry box. Kiran writes her bill as 3n + 2n - 6 + 2n rupees. (a) Write a correct expression for the bill. (b) Is Kiran's expression right? Explain his slip. (c) Find the bill when n = 40, and the amount by which Kiran's expression is wrong.
questions.a: (a) 3 notebooks cost 3n, 2 pens cost 2 × (n - 6) and the box costs 2n, so the bill is 3n + 2(n - 6) + 2n rupees (which is 7n - 12). (b) No. Kiran took ₹6 off only once, but each of the 2 pens is ₹6 cheaper, so ₹12 must come off. (c) Correct bill: 120 + 68 + 80 = ₹268. Kiran's expression gives 120 + 80 - 6 + 80 = ₹274, which is ₹6 too much.
s: (a) writes 3n + 2(n - 6) + 2n or an equal form
(b) says No and explains that ₹6 comes off for each of the 2 pens, not once
(c) finds ₹268 and shows Kiran's form gives ₹274, ₹6 more

questions.q: A photocopier takes 15 seconds to warm up once it is switched on, and then 3 seconds to print each page. Asha switches it on and prints 2 copies of a notice that has p pages. Which expression gives the time in seconds for the whole job?

For a family function of g guests, Hall A charges ₹2,000 for booking plus ₹150 for each guest. Hall B charges ₹5,000 for booking plus ₹120 for each guest. At either hall the caterer charges ₹220 for each guest, and the family spends ₹d on decoration. (a) Write an expression for the total cost in rupees at Hall A. (b) Write an expression for the total cost at Hall B. (c) Find both costs for 80 guests when d = 3,500. (d) Find both costs for 120 guests with the same d. (e) Work out both costs for 100 guests. The family is not yet sure how many guests will come. Use your answers to (c), (d) and (e) to advise them which hall to choose, and say whether d affects the choice.
questions.a: (a) 2000 + 150g + 220g + d, that is 2000 + 370g + d. (b) 5000 + 120g + 220g + d, that is 5000 + 340g + d. (c) Hall A: 2000 + 29,600 + 3,500 = ₹35,100; Hall B: 5000 + 27,200 + 3,500 = ₹35,700. Hall A is ₹600 cheaper. (d) Hall A: 2000 + 44,400 + 3,500 = ₹49,900; Hall B: 5000 + 40,800 + 3,500 = ₹49,300. Hall B is ₹600 cheaper. (e) At 100 guests Hall A costs 2000 + 37,000 + 3,500 = ₹42,500 and Hall B costs 5000 + 34,000 + 3,500 = ₹42,500, the same. Hall B costs ₹3,000 more for booking but ₹30 less per guest, so it gets better as the guest list grows: choose Hall A if they expect fewer than 100 guests and Hall B if more. d is the same at both halls and does not affect the choice.
s: (c) finds ₹35,100 and ₹35,700 for 80 guests
(d) finds ₹49,900 and ₹49,300 for 120 guests
(e) shows both cost ₹42,500 at 100 guests and advises Hall A below 100 guests and Hall B above, with d not affecting the choice

questions.q: True or False: On a city bus an adult ticket costs ₹12 and a child pays half of that. For a adults and c children travelling together, the total fare in rupees is 12(a + c) - 6. Test with 2 adults and 3 children, and give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. For 2 adults and 3 children the fare is 2 × 12 + 3 × 6 = ₹42, but 12(2 + 3) - 6 = ₹54. The expression charges everyone the full ₹12 and then takes off only one child's discount of ₹6; each child gets ₹6 off, so the fare is 12(a + c) - 6c, that is 12a + 6c rupees.
s: States False and shows the test: true fare ₹42 against ₹54 from the expression
Explains that ₹6 must come off for every child and writes 12(a + c) - 6c (or 12a + 6c)

questions.q:
Raghu is r years old. His sister is 4 years younger than him, and his father's age is 2 more than 3 times Raghu's age.
Statement 1: Five years from now, the father's age will be 3r + 7.
Statement 2: Four years from now, the sister will be r years old.
Statement 3: Five years ago, the father's age was 2 more than 3 times Raghu's age at that time.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: Tanu's piggy bank has x coins of ₹10, y coins of ₹5 and 12 coins of ₹2. (a) Write an expression for the money in the piggy bank in rupees. (b) Her father changes every ₹10 coin for two ₹5 coins. Write an expression for the number of coins now, and say whether the money in the bank has changed. (c) Find the money and the number of coins before and after the change when x = 7 and y = 9.
questions.a: (a) 10x + 5y + 24 rupees (12 coins of ₹2 make ₹24). (b) Each ₹10 coin becomes two ₹5 coins, so there are now 2x coins of ₹5 from the change, y old ₹5 coins and 12 coins of ₹2: 2x + y + 12 coins. The money does not change, because two ₹5 coins are worth one ₹10 coin. (c) Money: 70 + 45 + 24 = ₹139 both before and after. Coins: before 7 + 9 + 12 = 28, after 14 + 9 + 12 = 35.
s: (a) writes 10x + 5y + 24
(b) writes 2x + y + 12 coins and explains the money is unchanged
(c) finds ₹139, 28 coins before and 35 coins after

questions.q: A school club's account starts with ₹500. Each withdrawal takes out ₹120 and each deposit puts in ₹80, so after w withdrawals and d deposits the balance in rupees is 500 - 120w + 80d (a negative balance means the club owes the bank). (a) Find the balance after 6 withdrawals and 2 deposits, and say what it means. (b) The treasurer says that after 5 withdrawals, 1 deposit is enough to keep the club out of debt. Test this, and by trying d = 1, 2, ... find the fewest deposits that are enough.
questions.a: (a) 500 - 120 × 6 + 80 × 2 = 500 - 720 + 160 = -60. The club owes the bank ₹60. (b) With w = 5 and d = 1: 500 - 600 + 80 = -20, so the club still owes ₹20 and the treasurer is wrong. With d = 2: 500 - 600 + 160 = ₹60, so 2 deposits are the fewest that are enough.
s: (a) substitutes to get -60 and explains the club owes ₹60
(b) finds -20 for d = 1, says the treasurer is wrong, and finds d = 2 (₹60) is enough

questions.q: Raj says: 'Whatever number k stands for, the value of 7 - 2k is always less than 7.' Test his claim with k = 3, k = 0 and k = -3, and say whether he is right, wrong or only partly right.
questions.a: k = 3: 7 - 6 = 1, less than 7. k = 0: 7 - 0 = 7, not less than 7. k = -3: 7 - 2 × (-3) = 7 + 6 = 13, more than 7. So Raj is only partly right: 7 - 2k is less than 7 when k is a positive number, equal to 7 when k = 0 and more than 7 when k is negative, because subtracting a negative number adds.
s: Finds the value 1 for k = 3
Finds 7 for k = 0 and 13 for k = -3 with the signs handled correctly
Concludes partly right: true only for positive k, and gives the reason

questions.q: In a chess club league a player's points are 4w - 3l + d, where w is the number of games won, l the number lost and d the number drawn. Imran wins 5 games, loses 9 and draws 4. What are his points?

Look at the expression 3x - 2y. (a) Find its value for (x, y) = (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4) and (4, 5). (b) In each of these pairs y is 1 more than x. Describe the pattern in the values. (c) Without listing more pairs, predict the value for x = 50, y = 51, and check by substituting. (d) Replace y by x + 1 in 3x - 2y and simplify, to explain the pattern. (e) Use your answer to (d) to find the value for x = -3, y = -2, and check it by direct substitution.
questions.a: (a) 3 - 4 = -1, 6 - 6 = 0, 9 - 8 = 1, 12 - 10 = 2. (b) The values go up by 1 each time, and each value is 2 less than x. (c) Prediction 50 - 2 = 48; check: 150 - 102 = 48. (d) 3x - 2(x + 1) = 3x - 2x - 2 = x - 2, so whenever y is 1 more than x the value is x - 2. (e) x - 2 = -3 - 2 = -5; check: 3 × (-3) - 2 × (-2) = -9 + 4 = -5.
s: (b) says the value rises by 1 each time and is 2 less than x
(c) predicts 48 and checks 150 - 102 = 48
(d) simplifies 3x - 2(x + 1) to x - 2
(e) finds -5 both ways, with the signs handled

questions.q: A juice stall's profit in rupees for a day is 12a - (5b + 40), where a is the number of glasses sold, b is the number of glasses spilt, and ₹40 is the day's rent. (a) Find the profit on Monday, when a = 15 and b = 4. (b) Find the profit on Tuesday, when a = 8 and b = 6. (c) If one more glass is spilt and the sales stay the same, by how much does the profit change? Explain from the expression.
questions.a: (a) 12 × 15 - (5 × 4 + 40) = 180 - 60 = ₹120. (b) 12 × 8 - (5 × 6 + 40) = 96 - 70 = ₹26. (c) It falls by ₹5: increasing b by 1 makes the bracket 5 larger, and the whole bracket is subtracted.
s: (a) finds ₹120
(b) finds ₹26
(c) says the profit falls by ₹5 and explains using the bracket that is subtracted

questions.q:
Match each expression in Column I with its value for x = -3 in Column II.
Column I: 1. 2 - x  2. x - 2  3. -2x  4. 2(x + 1)
Column II: A. -5  B. -4  C. 5  D. 6

A printing press packs 25 copies of a magazine in each box. (a) Write the number of copies in n boxes in short form, and find it for 36 boxes. (b) A shop gets n boxes and 7 loose copies. A clerk writes the total as 25n7. Explain what is wrong and write the total correctly. (c) Find the correct total for n = 36.
questions.a: (a) 25n copies; for 36 boxes, 25 × 36 = 900. (b) In short form only the multiplication sign is left out, and the number is written in front of the letter. The 7 loose copies are added, so the total is 25n + 7; writing 25n7 hides the addition and puts a number after the letter. (c) 25 × 36 + 7 = 907 copies.
s: (a) writes 25n and finds 900
(b) explains the error and writes 25n + 7
(c) finds 907

questions.q:
Consider these statements about the short form of expressions.
Statement 1: 5 × m × 2 can be written in short form as 10m.
Statement 2: m × 7 + 3 is written in short form as m7 + 3.
Statement 3: When t = 0, the expression 8t has the value 8.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only

questions.q: An auditorium has three blocks of seats. Block A has r rows of 14 seats, Block B has r rows of 18 seats, and Block C has 6 rows of s seats. (a) Write the number of seats in each block in short form. (b) Write the total number of seats in its simplest form. (c) Find the total when r = 20 and s = 25. (d) For Block C, Arun writes s6 and Bela writes 6 + s. For s = 25, find what Bela's expression gives and explain why both are wrong ways to write the seats of Block C. (e) Two more rows are added to Block A and two to Block B. Write the new total and find by how many seats it has grown.
questions.a: (a) Block A: 14r, Block B: 18r, Block C: 6s. (b) 14r + 18r + 6s = 32r + 6s. (c) 32 × 20 + 6 × 25 = 640 + 150 = 790 seats. (d) Bela's 6 + s gives 31, but 6 rows of 25 seats are 6 × 25 = 150. Block C is 6 times s, not 6 more than s; and in short form the number comes first, so it is 6s, not s6. (e) 14(r + 2) + 18(r + 2) + 6s = 32r + 64 + 6s; the total grows by 64 seats (2 rows of 14 and 2 rows of 18).
s: (a) writes 14r, 18r and 6s
(b) writes 32r + 6s
(c) finds 790
(d) finds 31 against 150 and explains that 6s means 6 × s with the number first
(e) writes 32r + 64 + 6s (or an equal form) and finds 64 more seats

questions.q: A trader has 3 boxes of eggs and 2 loose eggs. Each box holds a trays and each tray holds b eggs, so she has 3ab + 2 eggs. How many eggs does she have when a = 4 and b = 6?

A bakery puts 6 buns in a packet and p packets on a tray. Rehan claims: 't trays hold 6pt buns, and if each tray held twice as many packets, the number of buns would also double.' (a) Explain why 6pt is the right short form for the buns in t trays. (b) Find the number of buns when p = 8 and t = 5. (c) Test the second part of his claim using 16 packets on each of the 5 trays. Is Rehan right?
questions.a: (a) Each tray holds 6 × p buns and t trays hold 6 × p × t buns; leaving out the signs and writing the number first gives 6pt. (b) 6 × 8 × 5 = 240 buns. (c) 6 × 16 × 5 = 480 buns, which is 2 × 240. In general 6 × 2p × t = 12pt, which is 2 times 6pt. Rehan is right on both parts.
s: (a) explains 6 × p × t written with the number first as 6pt
(b) finds 240
(c) finds 480, twice 240, and concludes Rehan is right

questions.q: True or False: Nisha writes 4 × a × 3 × b in short form as 43ab, and says its value is 860 when a = 2 and b = 10. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. Numbers can be multiplied in any order, so 4 × a × 3 × b = 4 × 3 × a × b = 12ab; the 4 and the 3 are multiplied, not written side by side as 43. For a = 2 and b = 10 the value is 12 × 2 × 10 = 240, not 860.
s: States False and writes the short form 12ab
Explains that 4 and 3 are multiplied, not joined into 43, and finds the value 240

questions.q: Asha scores m runs in her first innings of a season. Her next five innings are m + 7, m - 4, 2m, m - 9 and 2m + 6 runs. (a) Find the total of the six innings in simplest form. (b) Find the totals of the first three and of the last three innings, and how many more runs the last three gave, each in simplest form. (c) For m = 30, list the six scores, name the lowest and the highest, and check your answer to (a). (d) She then scores 3m - 5 in a seventh innings. Write the new total and find it for m = 30. (e) Her coach says the plain numbers made no difference to the six-innings total in (a). Explain why, and write that total if the fifth score m - 9 had been m - 5.
questions.a: (a) m + (m + 7) + (m - 4) + 2m + (m - 9) + (2m + 6) = 8m + 0 = 8m. (b) First three: 3m + 3. Last three: 5m - 3. Difference: (5m - 3) - (3m + 3) = 2m - 6 more runs. (c) 30, 37, 26, 60, 21, 66: lowest 21, highest 66; their total is 240 = 8 × 30. (d) 8m + 3m - 5 = 11m - 5; for m = 30 this is 325. (e) The plain numbers 7, -4, -9 and 6 add up to 0, so only 8m is left. With m - 5 in place of m - 9 they add up to 4, so the total would be 8m + 4.
s: (a) simplifies the total to 8m
(b) writes 3m + 3, 5m - 3 and the difference 2m - 6
(c) lists the scores, gives 21 and 66, and checks 240
(d) writes 11m - 5 and finds 325
(e) explains that 7, -4, -9, 6 add to 0 and writes 8m + 4

questions.q: A wall h metres high is painted in three side-by-side strips, 6 m, w m and 8 m wide, each running the full height. (a) Write the painted area in square metres in simplest form, and say why one of the terms cannot be joined to the others. (b) Find the area for h = 4 and w = 3.
questions.a: (a) 6h + wh + 8h = 14h + wh square metres. 6h and 8h are like terms and add to 14h, but wh has the letter-number w as well, so it is not a like term and stays separate. (b) 14 × 4 + 4 × 3 = 56 + 12 = 68 square metres.
s: (a) writes 14h + wh and explains that wh is not a like term of 6h and 8h
(b) finds 68 square metres

questions.q: A teacher asks which of these expressions can be cut down to just one term. Which one?

Neel says that 8x + 5 - 3x + 2y - 5 + y simplifies to 5x + 2y, and that the simplest form has 2 terms. (a) Group the like terms and simplify the expression. (b) Which parts of Neel's answer are right and which are wrong? (c) Check your answer with x = 1 and y = 1.
questions.a: (a) (8x - 3x) + (2y + y) + (5 - 5) = 5x + 3y. (b) Neel is partly right: the x-term 5x is right, the numbers 5 and -5 do cancel, and the simplest form does have 2 terms; but he missed the last y, so the y-term should be 3y, not 2y. (c) Original: 8 + 5 - 3 + 2 - 5 + 1 = 8; 5x + 3y = 8; Neel's 5x + 2y = 7.
s: (a) groups like terms and gets 5x + 3y
(b) says partly right: 5x and the 2 terms are right, the y-term is wrong
(c) shows the original and 5x + 3y both give 8 while Neel's gives 7

questions.q: A bangle shop sells glass bangles at ₹g a dozen and metal bangles at ₹m a dozen. On Monday it sold 5 dozen glass and 2 dozen metal bangles; on Tuesday 3 dozen glass and 7 dozen metal. On Wednesday a customer returned 1 dozen metal bangles bought on Tuesday and got her money back. What is the shop's money from these sales, in simplest form?
questions.a: 8g + 8m

questions.q: Pooja says: 'If an expression without brackets uses only the letter-numbers a and b and plain numbers, its simplest form can have at most 3 terms.' (a) Simplify 4a - 7 + 2b - a + 9 - 2b. (b) Is Pooja right? Explain using like terms.
questions.a: (a) (4a - a) + (2b - 2b) + (-7 + 9) = 3a + 0 + 2 = 3a + 2, which has only 2 terms. (b) Yes, Pooja is right. Every term is an a-term, a b-term or a plain number. All the a-terms are like terms and combine into one term, all the b-terms into one term and all the numbers into one number, so at most 3 terms remain; there can be fewer when a group adds up to 0, as the b-terms did in (a).
s: (a) simplifies to 3a + 2
(b) says Pooja is right
(b) explains that the a-terms, b-terms and numbers each combine into one term, so at most 3 remain

questions.q:
Consider these statements about removing brackets.
Statement 1: 3(2a - 5) - (a - 15) simplifies to 5a.
Statement 2: -(4 - y) + 4 simplifies to 8 - y.
Statement 3: 2(x + 3) - 2(x - 3) has the value 12 for every value of x.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: Find the two missing numbers so that 7p - (___p - ___) simplifies to 2p + 9. Show the simplification and check your answer with p = 3.
questions.a: Opening the bracket changes the sign of each term inside: 7p - (5p - 9) = 7p - 5p + 9 = 2p + 9, so the missing numbers are 5 and 9. Check with p = 3: 21 - (15 - 9) = 21 - 6 = 15, and 2 × 3 + 9 = 15.
s: Finds 5 by using 7p - 5p = 2p
Finds 9 by using that the minus sign makes -9 into +9
Checks with p = 3 that both sides give 15

questions.q: In a hockey practice match, a team gets m points for each goal and loses n points for each foul. Team Red's total is 9m - 2n - 5 and Team Blue's total is 4m - 7n + 3. (a) Write and simplify an expression for how many more points Red has than Blue. (b) Check your answer with m = 3 and n = 2.
s: (a) opens the bracket with every sign changed and gets 5m + 5n - 8
(b) finds 18 and 1, difference 17, matching 5m + 5n - 8 = 17

questions.q: Kavya has ₹500. A school bag is marked ₹p, and she gets ₹40 off, so she pays ₹(p - 40). Which expression, without brackets, gives the money she has left?

A school wants n banners printed each day for a sports week. Shop A's bill in rupees is 3(120n + 40) - (30n + 20): three days of printing at (120n + 40) rupees a day, less a discount of (30n + 20) rupees. Shop B's bill is 2(160n + 35) + 50: two days of faster printing at (160n + 35) rupees a day, plus ₹50 for delivery. (a) Simplify Shop A's bill. (b) Simplify Shop B's bill. (c) Use the simplest forms to find both bills for n = 1 and for n = 5. (d) Check Shop A's bill for n = 5 using the original form, working out the brackets first. (e) Advise the school which shop to choose, depending on n, and by trying n = 1, 2 and 3 find when the two bills match.
questions.a: (a) 360n + 120 - 30n - 20 = 330n + 100. (b) 320n + 70 + 50 = 320n + 120. (c) n = 1: A = 430, B = 440. n = 5: A = 1,750, B = 1,720. (d) 3 × (600 + 40) - (150 + 20) = 1,920 - 170 = 1,750. (e) Shop A starts ₹20 lower (100 against 120) but costs ₹10 more per banner (330 against 320). At n = 2 both bills are ₹760. So Shop A is cheaper for 1 banner a day, both are equal for 2, and Shop B is cheaper for 3 or more banners a day.
s: (a) simplifies Shop A to 330n + 100
(b) simplifies Shop B to 320n + 120
(c) finds 430 and 440 for n = 1, and 1,750 and 1,720 for n = 5
(d) gets 1,750 from the original form
(e) finds the bills equal at n = 2 (₹760) and advises A for 1 banner, B for 3 or more

questions.q: Arjun simplifies 15 - 2(3y - 4) like this: 15 - 2(3y - 4) = 15 - 6y - 8 = 7 - 6y. (a) Is his answer correct? Find the line with the mistake and explain it. (b) Write the correct simplest form. (c) Check with y = 2 by working out the bracket first in the original.
questions.a: (a) No. The first line is wrong: the -2 multiplies both terms in the bracket, and -2 × -4 = +8, so it should be 15 - 6y + 8. (b) 23 - 6y. (c) Original: 3 × 2 - 4 = 2, so 15 - 2 × 2 = 11. Correct form: 23 - 12 = 11. Arjun's form gives 7 - 12 = -5.
s: (a) says No and explains that -2 × -4 gives +8
(b) writes 23 - 6y
(c) gets 11 from the original and from 23 - 6y, and -5 from Arjun's form

questions.q: Divya puts y = 5 into 6(y - 1) and into 3y + 9, gets 24 from both, and says the two expressions are equal. (a) Test both expressions with y = 0. (b) Simplify 6(y - 1) and compare it with 3y + 9. (c) Is Divya right? What is wrong with her method?
questions.a: (a) At y = 0: 6(0 - 1) = -6, but 3 × 0 + 9 = 9. (b) 6(y - 1) = 6y - 6, which is not the same as 3y + 9. (c) No. Equal expressions must give the same value for every value of y; one value where they agree (y = 5) is not enough, and y = 0 shows they differ.
s: (a) finds -6 and 9 at y = 0
(b) simplifies to 6y - 6 and says it differs from 3y + 9
(c) says No and explains that agreeing at one value does not make expressions equal

questions.q: Look at the expressions 2(x + 3) + x and 4x + 1. (a) Make a table of the values of both expressions for x = 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. (b) Find the value of x, by continuing the table, at which the two values first become the same. (c) Which expression has the larger value at x = 3, and which at x = 8? (d) Simplify 2(x + 3) + x and use it to explain why the larger one changes as x grows. (e) Write an expression of the form (number)x + (number) that is equal to 2(x + 3) + x for every x.
questions.a: (a) 2(x + 3) + x: 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. 4x + 1: 1, 5, 9, 13, 17. (b) At x = 5 both give 21 (13 + 8 and 20 + 1). (c) At x = 3 the values are 15 and 13, so 2(x + 3) + x is larger; at x = 8 they are 30 and 33, so 4x + 1 is larger. (d) 2(x + 3) + x = 3x + 6. As x goes up by 1 it grows by 3 while 4x + 1 grows by 4, so 4x + 1 catches up at x = 5 and is bigger after that. (e) 3x + 6.
s: (a) gives both rows of the table correctly
(b) finds x = 5 with value 21
(c) finds 15 and 13 at x = 3, and 30 and 33 at x = 8, naming the larger each time
(d) simplifies to 3x + 6 and explains growth by 3 against growth by 4
(e) writes 3x + 6

questions.q: A cycle stand has b bicycles and t tricycles. Then 3 bicycles leave and 2 tricycles arrive. Which expression is NOT equal to the number of wheels in the stand now, for every b and t?
Show that 3(x + 2) and 3x + 2 can never take the same value, whatever number x stands for. Check your reason with x = 4 and x = -1.
questions.a: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6. Both expressions have the same 3x, and then one adds 6 while the other adds 2, so 3(x + 2) is always 4 more than 3x + 2 and they can never be equal. Check: x = 4 gives 18 and 14; x = -1 gives 3 and -1. Each time the difference is 4.
s: Opens the bracket to get 3x + 6
Explains that it is always 4 more than 3x + 2, so the values can never be equal

questions.q: Tanvi finds that 4(k - 2) and 4k - 2 are not equal. What single change to 4k - 2 makes it equal to 4(k - 2) for every value of k?
questions.a: Subtract 6

questions.q: (a) Find the values of 3(m + 4) - 2m and of m + 12 for m = 0, m = 5 and m = -3. (b) The values agree each time. Simplify 3(m + 4) - 2m to decide whether the two expressions are equal for every value of m.
questions.a: (a) m = 0: 12 and 12. m = 5: 27 - 10 = 17 and 17. m = -3: 3 - (-6) = 9 and 9. (b) 3(m + 4) - 2m = 3m + 12 - 2m = m + 12, the same expression, so they are equal for every value of m.
s: (a) finds 12, 17 and 9 for the first expression
(a) finds 12, 17 and 9 for m + 12
(b) simplifies to m + 12 and concludes they are equal for every m

questions.q: Squares are made from matchsticks in 2 rows, one row exactly above the other, with y squares in each row and shared sides using one matchstick. (a) Write an expression for the horizontal matchsticks. (b) Write an expression for the vertical matchsticks, and add the two to get the total in simplest form. Check it with y = 1. (c) Find all three counts for y = 20.
questions.a: (a) There are 3 horizontal lines of y matchsticks each: 3y. (b) There are (y + 1) vertical lines of 2 matchsticks each: 2(y + 1). Total: 3y + 2(y + 1) = 3y + 2y + 2 = 5y + 2. For y = 1: 3 + 4 = 7 and 5 + 2 = 7. (c) 60 horizontal, 42 vertical, 102 in all.
s: (a) writes 3y
(b) writes 2(y + 1), simplifies the total to 5y + 2 and checks 7 for y = 1
(c) finds 60, 42 and 102

questions.q: A science camp begins on a Wednesday, which is Day 1, and the days of the week repeat in a cycle of 7. On which day of the week does Day 100 of the camp fall?
questions.a: Thursday

questions.q: Farah says: 'The sum of any 4 numbers in a row, like 7, 8, 9, 10, is never a multiple of 4, but the sum of any 5 numbers in a row is always a multiple of 5.' (a) Test both parts once, using numbers of your choice. (b) Let the first number be n. Write the sum of 4 numbers in a row in simplest form and explain the first part. (c) Write the sum of 5 numbers in a row in simplest form and decide whether Farah is right.
questions.a: (a) For example 7 + 8 + 9 + 10 = 34, not a multiple of 4; 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 = 30, a multiple of 5. (b) n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) + (n + 3) = 4n + 6. 4n is a multiple of 4 and 6 is 2 more than the multiple 4, so the sum is always 2 more than a multiple of 4. (c) n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) + (n + 3) + (n + 4) = 5n + 10, which is 5 times n plus 5 times 2, so it is always a multiple of 5. Farah is right on both parts.
s: (a) tests one set of 4 and one set of 5 numbers correctly
(b) writes 4n + 6 and explains it is always 2 more than a multiple of 4
(c) writes 5n + 10, explains it is always a multiple of 5 and says Farah is right

questions.q: A garden path is laid in steps. At step y, a row of y white tiles is placed and grey tiles are laid all round it, so that the whole path is a rectangle 3 tiles wide and (y + 2) tiles long, with the white row in the middle. (a) Find the number of grey tiles at steps 1, 2, 3 and 4. (b) Leela counts the grey tiles as the full top row, the full bottom row and one tile at each end of the white row. Write her expression. (c) Mohan counts them as the tiles directly above and below the white tiles, plus the 3 tiles at each short end. Write his expression and show that it is equal to Leela's. (d) Find the grey tiles at step 25 and check your answer by finding all the tiles in the rectangle. (e) Grey tiles cost ₹15 each and white tiles ₹22 each. Write the cost of the tiles at step y in simplest form and find it for step 25.
questions.a: (a) 8, 10, 12, 14. (b) Leela: 2(y + 2) + 2. (c) Mohan: y + y + 3 + 3 = 2y + 6. Leela's opens to 2y + 4 + 2 = 2y + 6, the same. (d) 2 × 25 + 6 = 56 grey tiles. Check: the rectangle has 3 × 27 = 81 tiles, and 81 - 25 white = 56 grey. (e) 15(2y + 6) + 22y = 30y + 90 + 22y = 52y + 90; at step 25 this is 1,300 + 90 = ₹1,390.
s: (b) writes 2(y + 2) + 2
(c) writes 2y + 6 and shows Leela's simplifies to it
(d) finds 56 and checks with 81 - 25
(e) writes 52y + 90 and finds ₹1,390

questions.q: Flower pots are set out in a V. Step 1 has 2 pots at the point and 1 pot on each arm, and every new step adds 1 pot to each arm. Mohit counts 4 pots at step 1 and writes 4n for step n. Which expression is right?

Tiles are laid in a plus shape. At step y there is 1 centre tile with 4 arms (up, down, left, right) of y tiles each. (a) Write the tiles for steps 1, 2 and 3, and an expression for step y that follows the shape. (b) A second pattern is the same, except that the up and down arms each have (y + 1) tiles. Write its expression in simplest form, and say how the two patterns compare at every step. (c) Find the tiles at step 30 in both patterns.
questions.a: (a) 5, 9, 13. Step y: 1 + 4 × y = 4y + 1. (b) 1 + 2y + 2(y + 1) = 1 + 2y + 2y + 2 = 4y + 3. The second pattern always has 2 tiles more, one extra on each of the up and down arms. (c) 4 × 30 + 1 = 121 and 4 × 30 + 3 = 123.
s: (a) lists 5, 9, 13 and writes 4y + 1
(b) writes 4y + 3 and says it is always 2 more
(c) finds 121 and 123
